cues.en: All right.
In this lecture, we are going to look at which operations we can perform on cue.
Now these are the operations that we are going to perform in our upcoming lectures.
Now here we are just going to look at how they are working.
Now the first operation is enqueue operation.
Now we have mentioned that queue uses the Fifo method.
So this means that when we are enqueuing the elements to the queue, we are going to insert them after
each other.
So enqueue means that we are inserting new elements to the queue.
Now this is an empty queue over here.
Whenever we are inserting a new element, it's going to be inserted at the front of the queue.
Then when we insert the next element, it's going to insert it after the first element.
Then every time when we insert a new element, it's going to be inserted at the end of the queue because
queue uses the Fifo method.
So this means that the first element that comes will be removed first.
So that's why each element that comes after the current element is going to be inserted after that.
So this is how the logic of the enqueue method will work.
Now when it comes to the dequeue method, in this case, when we call the dequeue method for the queue,
it's going to remove the elements from the queue.
Now here we cannot remove the element from the middle of the queue or the end of the queue.
We have to remove the elements from the beginning of the queue.
So at the front we have ten.
So this means that whenever we are calling the dequeue method it's going to remove this element.
Then the other elements will be moved to the place of the first element.
Then the next element will be moved to the place of the first element and the third element will move
to the place of the second element and it continues like this.
Now, if I run the dequeue method one more time, so the front element is 20, it's going to be removed
and all other elements shifted one step.
Right.
So it will continue like this until we have removed all elements of the queue over here.
Now the next operation is front operation.
Now in some tutorials you will see that it's a peek.
In some tutorials you will see front.
So basically it's a front.
So whenever we are calling the front method it's going to return the front of the queue.
In this case it's going to be the ten.
And it will not remove this element from the beginning of the queue.
All it has to do is it's just going to return the first element from the queue.
Now the next operation is is empty method.
So it's empty method is obvious that it's going to return true or false.
So if the queue is empty it's going to return true.
If it is not it's going to return false.
So in this case we have elements in our queue.
It's going to return false.
Now the next method that we are going to implement is going to be the size method.
Now the size method returns the size of the queue.
So in this case we have five elements in the queue.
So that's why the size will return five.
Now at the end we will have clear method.
Now clear method means that whenever we are calling the clear method, it's going to delete all elements
of the queue.
And the queue will be empty.
So whenever we want to delete all elements of the queue, we just need to call the clear method.
Now let's go ahead and implement these methods one by one.
